podcast.body: Dazpán's third album, released in 2005, was a significant setback for the band, described as a "tremendous blow." It failed to win over the commercial audience that had been attracted by "bril," and critics no longer found it as interesting as "homburmo." The album was poorly received by both the public and critics, leaving the band in a precarious position, and notably, no tour followed its release. "se dieron una hostia tremenda salieron el 2005 y los pobres les fue bastante mal."

srcs.episode: Daft Punk y la historia de Alive 2007

podcast.body: Following "Discovery," Daft Punk's next album, "Human After All," was accompanied by an audiovisual project called "Electroma." "Tenemos los propios da punk y hicieron el electroma para el siguiente disco, que es Astroso, Human After all."

The third Daft Punk record was assembled in just six weeks and was considered fine but perhaps a little derivative and repetitive by fans. The subsequent Alive 2006–2007 tour, which featured the band performing in front of a giant LED-covered pyramid, was a massive success, especially in North America, and helped kick-start the entire EDM phenomenon on this side of the Atlantic. The live version of "Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger" was released as a single from the tour and netted Daft Punk Grammy Awards in 2008. Their performance with Kanye West at the 2008 ceremony was the first televised Daft Punk performance. "This tour, known as the Alive 2006-2007 tour, was a massive success, especially in North America."
